Canary thresholds and A/B routing plan
Cutover runbook responsibilities and quiet window
Security and audit log handoff for Private deployment

Action items assigned for smoke tests, audit log export, and a short trial of more aggressive KV prefix caching to reduce tail latency.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-10-02 14:30 PDT | Duration: ~48 minutes | Recording: yes
Attendees: Michael Park (Redwood AE), Anya Singh (Redwood SE), Ravi Menon (Redwood CSM), Tom Rivera (Nimbus Platform), Priya Kapoor (Nimbus Head of ML), Marcus Lee (CTO), Sara Cho (Security), Luis Fernandez (SRE)

[00:00] Michael: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got a packed agenda. Quick check — any blockers from last week's items?
[00:12] Tom: Uh, yeah we hit one thing in staging. The rollout script failed on a post-start hook intermittently, logs show a race with the sidecar. Luis is looking at it now.
[00:23] Luis: ack, it's a startup ordering issue on the infra template, i'll patch and re-run later today.
[00:30] Anya: Cool, thanks. For today's plan we want to go over the p95/p99 numbers, tuning notes from the KV prefix cache, and walk through the cutover runbook so roles are clear.
[00:42] Priya: also want to validate that the eval set we used covers our long-tail prompts, we saw a few hallucinations in the product messages.
[00:55] Michael: noted. quick metrics slide — (uh) overall token cost this week is down 12% after batching and quantization tweaks, p95 latency is 280ms, p99 is 620ms under the current staging load.
[01:10] Marcus: 620ms p99 — that's borderline for our interactive use case. Can we get that under 500?
[01:18] Anya: We have two levers. One: increase KV prefix caching so more sessions hit the cache — we saw p99 drop ~20% in a small test. Two: route longer context calls to the dedicated nodes with larger batch windows, trade a tiny bit of latency for throughput savings.
[01:35] Tom: Does routing to dedicated mean we need Dedicated Reserved capacity now? We were hoping to stay hosted for cost reasons.
[01:44] Michael: Not necessarily. We can do hybrid routing — keep majority on hosted, route heavy long-context calls to a smaller dedicated pool, or fall back to a smaller lower-cost model for non-critical requests.
[01:56] Priya: What's the cost delta look like — do we have numbers?
[02:01] Anya: In our sandbox A/B run, routing 15% of traffic to dedicated nodes increased infra cost but reduced overall token cost by ~6% because of fewer retries and better batching. I'll attach the cost table after the call.
[02:18] Ravi: Also flagged: you asked for an SLA on latency, we should align on which metric we gate the cutover with — p95 or a combined error+latency signal.
[02:27] Michael: Suggestion — use a compound gate: p95 < 350ms AND error rate < 0.5% for 30 minutes during the quiet window. If either trips, auto rollback.
[02:40] Marcus: That seems reasonable. What about canary thresholds?
[02:44] Anya: Propose a 4-step canary: 1) 1% for 15 minutes smoke, 2) 10% for 30 minutes monitoring response patterns, 3) 50% for 1 hour with throttles, 4) full. Each step requires N metrics to be green: p95, p99 trend no >20% increase, error rate, and business signal (conversational completion rate).
[03:07] Tom: For the canary automation, do we have playbooks to manually abort? 
[03:11] Michael: Yes — runbook includes manual abort commands and an automated circuit breaker tied to the telemetry cluster — threshold triggers roll back to previous model variant.
[03:21] Priya: On telemetry, we need traces with token-level timing, not just aggregated latencies. Will Redwood provide trace spans we can ingest into our tracing system?
[03:31] Anya: Yes, we export OpenTelemetry spans. We'll enable token timing spans for the pilot canary and share the Jaeger/tempo endpoint sample.
[03:40] Sara: From security: we need audit log samples and proof of KMS calls for key usage. Also need to validate SAML SSO for admin console before any Private deployment.
[03:51] Michael: We can export a 7-day audit sample. KMS is integrated — we'll provide a playbook and a sample key rotation event. SAML SSO is part of the Private checklist.
[04:02] Sara: Cool. Also any PII retention notes — do you redact prompt inputs in logs?
[04:08] Anya: By default logs contain request IDs and metadata, we can configure redaction or hashing of input text before it lands in long-term storage. That's in the data retention page I'll link.
[04:20] Luis: quick infra question — if we hit a noisy neighbor on shared hosted, how does the fallback work?
[04:25] Michael: Smart routing will detect capacity anomalies and shift traffic to either reserved pool or to a smaller model variant with similar quality (we call those compatible fallbacks). We can set policy thresholds.
[04:37] Priya: about quality — earlier you mentioned more aggressive quantization saved cost but increased some token-level noise. Is there a recommended quantization profile for our domain?
[04:48] Anya: For retail conversational templates we recommend per-channel 8-bit quant with a small calibration set. It lowers memory and tends to keep BLEU/ROUGE metrics stable; we'll add the calibration notes.
[04:57] Michael: Ok let's walk through the cutover runbook now — I'll read out the high-level steps and assign owners.
[05:03] Michael: Step 0: Preflight — ensure staging runbook complete, smoke tests green, audit samples delivered. Owner: Nimbus (Tom/Luis).
[05:12] Michael: Step 1: Quiet window kickoff — 2 hours starting at T0, no other infra changes. Owner: Nimbus SRE (Luis).
[05:19] Michael: Step 2: Canary ramp — follow 1/10/50/100 plan, automation will check gates every 15 minutes. Owner: Redwood SE (Anya) + Nimbus Platform (Tom).
[05:29] Michael: Step 3: Full cutover and validation — monitor business signals for 2 hours, if stable promote. Owner: Marcus + Michael.
[05:36] Marcus: If something goes sideways during the 50% step, what's the rollback latency?
[05:41] Anya: The rollback path is immediate — we keep the previous model pinned and can re-route within 30s; traffic reconvergence takes ~2-3 minutes to stabilize.
[05:49] Tom: Do we have runbook commands? I want a one-click abort.
[05:53] Michael: Yes, the runbook includes an abort script in the Redwood console that triggers circuit breaker, re-pins previous variant and notifies the Slack channel.
[05:59] Priya: On monitoring thresholds — we want to add a business metric: completion accuracy on a holdout set every 10 minutes. Can we compute that in near-real-time?
[06:08] Anya: We can run a minibatch evaluator against new responses and report an accuracy score; it's not perfect but will surface regressions quickly.
[06:15] Marcus: Good. For the quiet window timing — what time zone do we pick? Our EU traffic is higher daytime but US has the majority of active sessions.
[06:24] Michael: Recommend starting at 22:00 UTC to catch low-volume global window; we can coordinate a 2-hr block.
[06:31] Luis: staging smoke — i'll re-run the script after patching startup order, and post results.
[06:36] Tom: Regarding the KV prefix cache test, what exact config did you change?
[06:40] Anya: We increased prefix length retention from 2 to 6 and bumped cache hotness TTL from 30s to 120s; that reduced the number of KV misses on session join.
[06:50] Priya: Did that affect cold-start memory or evictions?
[06:53] Anya: Slightly higher memory but still under cap for the dedicated instances we test. We can revert if we see eviction storms.
[06:59] Michael: Any other security blockers?
[07:02] Sara: need to validate the RBAC roles for the console — admin vs ops vs viewer — and make sure logs are tamper-evident. I'll sign off once audit sample looks good.
[07:10] Michael: Great. Now a short Q&A and then we'll call out owners.
[07:15] Marcus: One more: do you support a blue/green style switch instead of canary for us? Given our architecture, blue/green might be simpler.
[07:23] Anya: We do support blue/green; tradeoff is traffic cut is bigger risk but rollback is straightforward. Given your business signal gating needs, canary is safer but we can do blue/green for a second attempt if canary stalls.
[07:36] Tom: Ok let's stick to canary for the first go.
[07:40] Michael: Recap of owners: Anya runs A/B load test and KV tuning; Tom/Luis run staging smoke and idempotency; Sara validates KMS and audit; Michael publishes runbook; Priya to validate eval set and holdout metrics.
[07:56] Priya: I'll also prepare a short prompt set for the minibatch evaluator.
[08:01] Michael: Alright, closing — we'll share the runbook link by Monday, and schedule the go/no-go for 2026-10-08. Thanks everyone.
[08:08] (end recording)
